text.p: Tropical storm Peter is expected to make landfall along the northwest coast of Kyushu Japan, north of Nagasaki, in less than 12 hours. The main problem due to this system will be a strong coastal storm surge leading to flooding. Western Kyushu Japan will be hardest hit. Winds up to 65 mph will also cause damage as the system comes across the coast line. Heavy rains will also cause flooding as the system moves westward from Kyushu to Honshu Japan during the weekend. Winds will diminish but strong gusts are still possible during this time.

Torrential rains continue to impact the Gujarat area of India. The city of Ahmadhabad has received at least 21.00 inches of rain during the past 7 days and is now 676 percent of normal for the month to date. Widespread and severe flooding has already been reported in the region and this should get worse before it gets any better. Floods will likely cause extreme damage in the region, which may include agriculture. Major crops in the area include cotton, sorghum and groundnuts.
There are no further statements at this time.
